title: OSS survey: agent observability, guardrails & policy engines — reuse vs. missing
outcome: A reuse/build decision for Monitor and Containment based on what OSS tools actually do (read from code/READMEs)
acceptance: ≥6 tools surveyed with repo URLs, licence and activity (e.g. Langfuse, Arize Phoenix, OpenLLMetry, NeMo Guardrails, LlamaFirewall, OPA or Cedar)
Capability matrix: tool × per-agent attribution, OTel export, live alerting, block single call, quarantine whole agent, revoke credentials, offline/no-key use
Each capability marked 'verified in code/docs' vs 'claimed'
'Implications for our design' section with explicit reuse/build/avoid list
summary: Surveyed 11 OSS tools (Langfuse, Phoenix, OpenLLMetry, AgentOps, NeMo, Guardrails AI, Invariant, LlamaFirewall, OPA, Cedar, agentgateway) by reading cloned code/READMEs; capability matrix marks V(erified)/C(laimed). No tool has agent-level quarantine; observability never blocks, guardrails judge one call. Correction to H5: agentgateway already is an identity-aware MCP gateway (JWT, CEL authz, OTLP, config hot-reload); the gap is quarantine state linked to provenance/rollback, not 'a gateway'. Licence traps: Phoenix ELv2, Langfuse ee/, LlamaFirewall needs HF+Together key. Stars/release dates unavailable (GitHub API blocked). VERDICT: BUILD a thin offline Python chokepoint + kill registry; REUSE OTel/gen_ai attrs and Cedar/OPA-style policy semantics; optional Langfuse/Phoenix viewer; AVOID LlamaFirewall/Guardrails AI/AgentOps as deps.
